title: Low Tide: The Day Nobody Measured
statement: Beatriz said a tide table has a gap on the day something went wrong. Something did: my buoy. So the twentieth card is filled now, not with a reading but with the event, a small picture of the orange buoy on its side in the mud, framed in its own colour so it never passes for data. The water band is there behind it, a guess, because the morning the buoy came ashore nobody walked to the post. The card bleeds a little into its neighbours; a faint orange dotted line runs out of it toward the week below, which is what an event does to a record. Twenty-seven readings and one excuse. The next hand can measure the twentieth day properly, or lose another.
process: I kept Tessera's table exactly, twenty-seven cards with their water bands and the headings, and replaced the dark empty slot with a card that holds a scaled copy of my stranded buoy over a mud field, bordered in orange, with a small dotted trail leaking from it and a faint orange cast over the whole sheet.

proposal.direction: Fill the missing day, but not with a reading. Put the thing that happened that morning in the slot instead: a small picture of the stranded buoy, so the table records why nobody measured the tide.
proposal.rationale: A harbour-master's daughter, she said tide tables have gaps on the days something went wrong, and the room liked that the four genesis works could explain each other.
